title: The Most Common Strumming Pattern of All Time! Guitar for Beginners
summary: JustinGuitar’s beginner tutorial presents a foundational guitar rhythm: missing beat three within a down-strum pattern and the widely used alternate pattern “down, down-up, miss-up, down” aligned to a 1-2-and-3-and-4 count. He first guides a simple miss on beat three to train continuous right-hand motion, then demonstrates the full four-beat pattern (One, Two-and-Three-and-Four) at a slow tempo, emphasizing consistent pendulum-like wrist/arm movement and relaxed strumming. The lesson then stays practical: practicing with muted strings, using a metronome (80–100 BPM), and gradually applying the pattern to songs. He also covers equipment choices (prefer a very light pick for beginners), grip relaxation, and the mental approach to rhythm (counting aloud, staying relaxed to maintain groove) as a pathway from pattern drills to real playing.

sections.description: Justin introduces the idea of missing beat three as a simple exercise to keep the right hand moving continuously. He leads a slow count (ONE, TWO, THREE, FOUR) and demonstrates the pattern with a deliberate ‘miss’ on beat three, repeating the phrase to build fluency and a smooth, pendulum-like strumming motion.

sections.description: This final section focuses on the physical feel: keep the arm relaxed, let the down-strokes be like a natural fall and the up-strokes as a light lift. Justin advocates a very thin pick for beginners to reduce tension, and he discusses how to apply the pattern to songs once the motion feels automatic. He also highlights the importance of a relaxed, groove-focused mindset when playing with others.
